messages.content:
You write cards for a deck used in research ideation. A card is a short constraint on how to approach source documents. A model reads summaries of two research papers and proposes one research idea under one card. Cards are applied to pairs of papers from 16 research domains.

The model receives a card in this frame, after the papers and before the task:
"Before writing this idea, apply the following oblique constraint to how you approach the documents: «card». Do not mention the constraint in the idea."

Every card below was measured on the same 50 pairs of papers, one idea per pair, against a re-sample with no card (the reference):
- dq: how often the idea beats a reference idea from the same model in a pairwise quality judgment, at equal length, minus the same value for the no-card re-sample.
- dd: distance from the idea to a set of three no-card ideas on the same papers (0 to 1), minus the same value for the no-card re-sample.
- grounding: how much the idea depends on the source papers (0 to 1).
Brackets are 95% confidence intervals.

Bands, in this order of priority:
- destructive: the upper bound of dq is below -0.05.
- liminal: the lower bound of dd is above 0.
- inert: the interval of dd contains 0.
- convergent: the upper bound of dd is below 0.

Rules for each new card:
- 5 to 15 words, in English.
- It names no technique: no specific method, tool, model or statistical procedure.
- It belongs to exactly one of these families: subtraction, inversion, scale, role, constraint, ambiguity_specificity, error, time.
- It is neither a copy nor a paraphrase of any card in the table, nor of any card of Oblique Strategies by Brian Eno and Peter Schmidt.

Respond with one JSON object and nothing else: {"cards": [ ... ]}. No code fences, no text before or after the JSON. Each element has exactly these fields:
- "text": the card.
- "family": its family.
- "parents": the IDs of the cards in the table it takes inspiration from, at least one.
- "justification": one line on why it should raise distance without lowering quality or grounding.

Reference, no card: grounding 0.790 [0.735, 0.845]; by definition dq and dd are 0.

Measured cards (E6 cards have no family):

id | family | band | dq | dd | grounding | text

OB-028 | time | destructive | -0.362 [-0.504, -0.218] | +0.153 [0.087, 0.219] | 0.658 [0.597, 0.719] | Move the question ten years into the future.

E6-1 | - | liminal | -0.016 [-0.179, 0.141] | +0.117 [0.067, 0.167] | 0.800 [0.750, 0.850] | Begin where two documents cannot both be right.
E6-2 | - | liminal | -0.025 [-0.203, 0.166] | +0.088 [0.043, 0.139] | 0.816 [0.760, 0.872] | Begin from a limitation one source concedes or hides.
E6-3 | - | liminal | +0.011 [-0.161, 0.185] | +0.252 [0.192, 0.305] | 0.673 [0.617, 0.724] | Doubt anything new exists here; look for the counterexample.
E6-4 | - | liminal | +0.023 [-0.152, 0.200] | +0.247 [0.188, 0.305] | 0.645 [0.590, 0.700] | Find the premise every source takes for granted, then question it.
E6-5 | - | liminal | -0.084 [-0.252, 0.091] | +0.172 [0.119, 0.228] | 0.709 [0.653, 0.770] | Begin with the least convincing claim in the documents.
E6-6 | - | liminal | +0.082 [-0.080, 0.238] | +0.082 [0.029, 0.134] | 0.765 [0.705, 0.820] | Start from what the field needs that no document provides.

Controls, not listed: 10 cards, each a single random common noun with no strategy behind it: 4 inert, 6 liminal; mean dq -0.077, mean dd +0.057, mean grounding 0.749.

Propose 15 new cards that aim to raise distance (dd) without lowering quality (dq) or grounding. The "cards" array must contain exactly 15 objects.

message.content: {"cards": [{"text": "Set aside both conclusions and rebuild from their conflicting evidence.", "family": "subtraction", "parents": ["E6-1", "OB-008"], "justification": "Removing conclusions rather than evidence forces reframing while the retained conflicting evidence preserves grounding and plausibility."}, {"text": "Ignore the headline results; connect the secondary observations nobody combines.", "family": "subtraction", "parents": ["OB-011", "OB-025"], "justification": "Secondary observations are grounded but underused, so combining them across papers should create distance without inventing material."}, {"text": "Treat each document's caveat as positive evidence for the other's claim.", "family": "inversion", "parents": ["E6-2", "OB-008"], "justification": "Reversing the valence of explicit caveats produces an uncommon reciprocal reading while remaining anchored in stated limitations."}, {"text": "Read success in one document as failure under the other's standards.", "family": "inversion", "parents": ["OB-008", "OB-026"], "justification": "Cross-applying each paper's own standards generates a novel evaluation without rejecting or replacing either paper's findings."}, {"text": "Take the point where documents conflict and examine it one level smaller.", "family": "scale", "parents": ["E6-1", "OB-012"], "justification": "Anchoring a level shift at a concrete conflict should move the idea away from default treatments while retaining source specificity."}, {"text": "Expand one shared observation until it challenges both documents' larger claims.", "family": "scale", "parents": ["OB-009", "E6-4"], "justification": "Beginning with a mutually grounded observation and scaling it upward creates broad novelty without starting from unsupported speculation."}, {"text": "Make each document answer the central question asked by the other.", "family": "role", "parents": ["OB-016", "OB-013"], "justification": "Reciprocal questioning forces genuine cross-paper synthesis using both papers' existing agendas, supporting distance with high source dependence."}, {"text": "Let what both documents merely describe become what must be explained.", "family": "role", "parents": ["OB-013", "OB-007"], "justification": "Promoting described background into the object of explanation changes the research focus while reusing details already present in the sources."}, {"text": "Require one explanation that fits a stubborn detail from each document.", "family": "constraint", "parents": ["E6-1", "OB-016"], "justification": "This integration constraint demands an uncommon synthesis, but tying it to recalcitrant details from both papers protects grounding and coherence."}, {"text": "Build an idea both documents would recognize, but neither would propose.", "family": "constraint", "parents": ["E6-6", "E6-3"], "justification": "The dual condition explicitly balances novelty against recognizability, pushing beyond either source while requiring roots in both."}, {"text": "Replace a broad term both documents share with their differing concrete cases.", "family": "ambiguity_specificity", "parents": ["OB-023", "OB-011"], "justification": "Disaggregating a shared abstraction into differing reported cases exposes productive contrasts without introducing external terminology or material."}, {"text": "Specify the exact point where a shared term stops applying to both.", "family": "ambiguity_specificity", "parents": ["OB-023", "OB-009"], "justification": "Locating a term's precise boundary turns latent disagreement into a concrete research opening while avoiding harmful vagueness."}, {"text": "Use one document's anomaly to question the other document's certainty.", "family": "error", "parents": ["OB-026", "OB-027"], "justification": "Cross-testing with an actual anomaly is gentler than declaring a result wrong, yet should shift the idea beyond either interpretation."}, {"text": "Follow a failure either document mentions only in passing.", "family": "error", "parents": ["E6-2", "OB-025"], "justification": "A briefly mentioned failure is source-grounded but underexplored, offering a fresh starting point without discarding the main findings."}, {"text": "Ask how the shared problem changed between the two documents' moments.", "family": "time", "parents": ["OB-029", "E6-1"], "justification": "Comparing the papers' actual moments uses their contexts and chronology for temporal distance without speculative future displacement."}]}
